result.score_rationale: All five §4 combat-core blockers (reach cap, crit read, early TTK, multi-target rule, crit gating) are closed at literal decompiled source, plus three §1 UNKNOWN-UNKNOWNS (multi-target damage rule, reach-cap↔dash relationship, hit-registration window) and half of a fourth (i-frames). Held off the 90s by four things: (a) every source cite is the ANDROID v0.682 client and parity with the web v0.717 is unproven — and already broken once, measured on frames (claim crit-meter-fill-rate); (b) duel AI/telegraphs live in EnemyPlayer.as/Enemy*.as, surveyed by L4 not here; (c) screen-shake, hitstop-beyond-i-frames and blend modes still uncatalogued; (d) three live constants in src/config/reach.ts and one in src/config/stances.ts are WRONG against the source and must be fixed before any of it is wired in.

result.score_rationale: Ledger says 34/100. Re-scored 78. All five §4 blockers resolve on disk: ① the level→stat formula is NPC.setLevel() (linear rescale + 0.9 sub-21 + a hard 1/1/1 clamp at lvl<=10); ② 403 authored <hp> rows (1..1000); ③ every attack animation ships as parta/partb/partc with explicit frame durations across 471 timed anims; ④ per-class engagement distances (50/100/400/250) plus a 24-frame decision cadence, and 118 <wave> blocks with 160 <x> spawn coords + drop-in-from-above rule; ⑤ the archer's full ballistic solve (GRAVITY=3, cos30 launch, ±4 jitter) and — refuting the blocker's premise — no reflect mechanic anywhere, only a zombie half-damage-unless-behead gate. Beyond the blockers the payload holds a 38-case ai-id→class dispatch that the shipped 3-tier AI_TIERS does not model at all. Capped at 78, not 90+, by four things: (1) every behavioural constant comes from the ANDROID v0.682 decompile — the web v0.717 payload decompile holds 652 classes and ZERO Enemy*/NPC* gameplay code, so build parity is unestablished and this is the dominant residual risk; (2) "Tengu", listed Ready in the ledger taxonomy, greps to 0 across the entire payload and script tree; (3) the 38 behaviour classes are unwritten work, not a tuning gap; (4) the 12-frame hit-lockout is a counter with no stagger animation and wants frame-side confirmation before it is treated as CONTRACT.

claims.text: The enemy level→stat formula the ledger calls "absent, not just inferred" is NPC.setLevel(): a linear rescale of the authored XML statline (factor = requestedLvl / authoredLvl, ×0.9 at or under level 20) applied identically to damage, defense and maxhp, with a hard clamp to 1/1/1 at level ≤ 10 and xp = lvl*2 + 20.
claims.quote: public function setLevel(lvl:int) : * { var factor:Number = lvl / this.level; if(lvl <= 20) { factor *= 0.9; } this.level = lvl; this.damage *= factor; this.defense *= factor; maxhp *= factor; setHP(maxhp); this.updateHealthBar(); this.xp = lvl * 2 + 20; if(lvl <= 10) { this.damage = 1; this.defense = 1; maxhp = 1; setHP(maxhp); } }

Every one of the five named blockers in the "### art-anim-audio-feel — 56" block is now resolved: (1) ALL AUDIO is recovered as 26 playable MP3 masters plus the complete mixing/trigger contract; (2) the font is identified down to its embedded font program and vendor copyright string; (3) "FX blend modes" is answered — the game sets NO blendMode anywhere, all compositing is ColorTransform + BlurFilter + ColorMatrixFilter via one small class; (4) screen-shake is fully catalogued (exact algorithm, default amplitude 30, trigger set); (5) the severed-limb death is not one variant but a gore SYSTEM with a measured 40/20/20/20 distribution, a behead flag, and a global censor switch. On top of that the animation model is settled from bytes (24 Hz keyframe stream, 21-node rig, code-added hold tails) and 14 of 18 animation blobs are proven byte-identical between the Android and web builds, so the usual Android caveat does not apply to motion. Held back from higher: the newly-opened vector art (1,949 sprites in SHS3Resource, 49 backgrounds in BGResource) was not rendered or graded this pass; audio web-parity is unproven (the web payload holds no CWS blob at all); and no test in the suite pins any of this yet.

result.score_rationale: Pass 1 of this lane already moved ui-hud 57 -> 85 on the Android decompile; I re-derived its claims 1-18 independently and they hold, so 85 is the floor, not a contested number. +3 for three things Pass 1 left open or got wrong: (a) blocker (5) goes from "half closed" to "closed except symbol geometry" — DialogBox re-assigns its layout in ActionScript every show (button.x 340 / 270+425, msgText.y 187.5 vs 220, centre-if-<=2-lines), and the battle pause is a full behaviour spec (button hidden in duel/PvP, pauseScreen raised to top, any click resumes); (b) the screen-transition durations Pass 1 declared "unheld pending a follow-up" are constants in the same file and resolve by arithmetic to 17 frames / 708 ms for each shutter and exactly 24 frames / 1000 ms for the white fade; (c) an entire UI subsystem — 19-screen, 47-menu, 139-option InteractUI UIData with inventory gates and error copy — is on disk and appears in neither the ledger nor Pass 1. Held below 90 by real gaps, not caution: no assets.swf symbol geometry exported (BattleUI symbol2952, OptionsUI symbol1133, DialogBox symbol83, SkillSlotButton symbol2915 etc. are script-only exports), no icon manifest for the 139 icon ids, HUD chrome art still sealed in the encrypted 124_Mobile_ImageResource, the 800x690 friend-bar layout is code-held but appears in zero reference frames, and "(EQ:n) UX" is still ungrounded. Separately, P1 is a correctness hit that does not change the score but changes every other lane: the string-id mapping Pass 1 used is the wrong one.

claims.text: Screen-transition durations are constants in the shipped code and resolve exactly: each black shutter takes 17 frames (708 ms) and the white fade takes exactly 24 frames (1000 ms) at the SWF's 24 fps.
claims.quote: `this.blackup.y = -240; this.blackdown.y = 480; this.blackMovtSpeed = 0; this.counter = 0;` (:143-146) then per frame `this.blackup.y += this.blackMovtSpeed; this.blackdown.y -= this.blackMovtSpeed; this.blackMovtSpeed += 2; if(this.blackup.y >= 0){ this.blackup.y = 0; this.blackdown.y = 240; if(this.counter >= 17)` (:80-88), and `this.white.alpha -= 1 / 24;` (:111). Speed applies before it increments, so displacement after n frames is (n-2)(n-1); (17-2)(17-1) = 240 exactly, which is why the gate is counter >= 17.

result.score_rationale: 31/100 is badly stale. Of the four §4 blockers: ② (map topology) is fully closed at BOTH scales — a 6×6 sector board plus a world board that is a 63×72 GIF byte-identical across the web and Android payloads (735 land territories); ③ (achievements / daily-reward / token numbers) is closed outright with 61 resolved achievements, the full 36/6/10-slot daily prize tables, and both token pools quantified; ① (server sim) is closed on MECHANICS (deploy = 100×terrain-mod, arrows = 80+rand40×mod, 7-row terrain table, structure costs, 11-rank curve, 24h advance, 39-wave battle table) and open only on hosted state; ④ (offline gold faucet) is NOT unclosable as both the ledger and the first survey pass claimed — doRebirth grants 5 Gold per rebirth and 20 at Dan 8, a 60-Gold lifetime ceiling the client itself uses as its paid-player test. verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/Damage.as:149-170 (getMinDamage) + reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/MCSPlayer.as:3415-3418 (call site)
verdicts.reason: The ledger bullet 'defense min-floor (EnemyLevel/4)' is CORRECT and the surveyor cited the wrong function. Damage.getMinDamage() IS the generic defense-pipeline floor: 'if(attackerlvl<=10) return 1+piercing; if(<=20) return attackerlvl/8+piercing; if(<=30) return attackerlvl/6+piercing; return attackerlvl/4+piercing;' and MCSPlayer.as applies it immediately after 'damage -= this.getDefense();' -> 'if(damage < damageObj.getMinDamage()) damage = damageObj.getMinDamage();'. For incoming damage attackerlvl IS the enemy's level, so at lvl>30 the floor is literally EnemyLevel/4. The same floor is applied at 10+ further receipt sites (EnemyWolf.as:384, EnemyShield.as:347, EnemyClone.as:222/:443, EnemyNianMonster.as:383, MCSPlayer.as:3710). The surveyor's EnemyPlayer.as:107-123 block is real (I confirmed it verbatim) but computes 'bossHP = playerhit * hitsToKillBoss' -- enemy HP auto-scaling, copy-pasted into EnemySpearElite.as:107, EnemyWolfAlpha.as:109, EnemyKanjiGuardian.as:88, EnemyElite.as:63. So 'wrong in both variable and shape' is false twice: the shape is identical (the ledger recorded the top band), and the generic pipeline really is keyed to enemy level. Acting on this correction would delete a correct L1/L2 rule.

verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/MCSItem.as:203-224 (setConsumable) and :226-247 (setAccessory); corroborated by my own crop of reference/frames/s21_weapon/t708.0.png (900,590)-(1640,960) upscaled x2 LANCZOS

verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/ShopItem.as:51-52 (`this.borderType = itemRef.getShopItemType(); gotoAndStop(this.borderType + "_default");`) and reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/GameEngine.as:567 (`str = "Tip: A blue border indicates that an item is rare.";`)
verdicts.reason: BACKWARDS. The border IS the 4-tier ladder. ShopItem.as:51 sets borderType from getShopItemType() - the same four-valued function (unique/rare/special/normal) the surveyor quoted in claim 12 - and gotoAndStop(borderType + "_default") means the border art has four frames: normal_default, special_default, rare_default, unique_default. Purple is simply the TOP TIER's border, not a separate flag. The refutation sits FOUR LINES ABOVE the tip the surveyor cited: GameEngine.as:567 reads "Tip: A blue border indicates that an item is rare." - proving borders exist for other tiers. Two further errors ride along: (a) getShopItemType() returns "unique" on itemxml.unique==1 OR isPickableQuestItem() OR the five trade-quest IDs OR isPlayerNamed(), so it is not "the <unique> flag" even at the top tier; (b) <unique> is not boolean - I counted 253 <unique>1 and 116 <unique>2 rows in itemdata.xml, and every code test is ==1. The lane_impact is inverted: following it, a builder DELETES the blue rare and green special borders the game ships. Frame check: my inventory crop (900,590)-(1640,960) x2 shows 2 of 7 icons purple-bordered and 5 plain - no rare/special item is in this bag, so the frame is SILENT between the two hypotheses and the code is the authority.

verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/MCSCharacter.as:120 (`internal var partListLength:int = 22;`) with :141 (`for(var i:int = 0; i <= this.partListLength; i++)`), :56-62 (PART_l_shoulder/r_shoulder/l_knee/r_knee declared `:*` = 23/24/25/26), MCSWolf.as:188 + :197 (their only consumers), and MCSCharacter.as:915-1088 setArmor

verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/Item.as:1582-1593 AND :1564-1580 (`return this.weight * this.getQuantity();`) vs web v0.717 reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/§1t17s0§.as:1977-1988 AND :1958-1975 (`return (this.weight + this.§1t478s0§) * this.§1t484s0§();`)
verdicts.reason: HELD on the formula - I read both builds and getSellAmt is byte-identical in shape (id<3000 -> 1; getWeight()>=10 -> (1+modcount)*10; else *5). The cite lines are exact in both. BUT the cross-build parity assertion overreaches: getWeight(), the input to the formula's only branch, DIVERGES between builds. Android returns `this.weight * this.getQuantity()`; web v0.717 returns `(this.weight + this.§1t478s0§) * this.§1t484s0§()` - an extra per-item weight term with no Android counterpart. So 'confirmed in BOTH builds' holds for getSellAmt and fails for the quantity that decides its branch; the S0-3 parity caveat is still live here, not discharged. Also under-specified in a way that changes numbers: getWeight() multiplies by QUANTITY, so >=10 is a STACK threshold, not an item-weight threshold - ten weight-1 items sell at x10, not x5. Not refuted (the formula is right and verbatim), but the 'exactly and in BOTH builds' framing needs the caveat restored.

new_findings.text: The elemental AoE parameter is a horizontal half-width, not a radius: the hit test compares x-distance only, so Inferno 600 / Tsunami 400 / Tornado 200 / Earthquake 50 describe a band +/-N px wide with unbounded y.

new_findings.text: Defense is subtracted from the physical damage term only — fire, wind, water and earth damage are added after the min-damage floor and are never mitigated by DEF; and a behead multiplies x1.5 after the floor too.

new_findings.text: Two more web-vs-android divergences in the same function: the web anti-cheat rejects a jump of more than 2 levels (android: 5 or more), and the web build has consoleEnabled constant-folded to a literal false, so every guard written !consoleEnabled is unconditional in v0.717.

GAUNTLET-WIDE decoding rule: whenever an android guard reads `!consoleEnabled && X`, the web equivalent is plain `X` — do not port the flag, and do not treat an android console/admin path as evidence that a behaviour was reachable in v0.717.

verdicts.reason: REFUTED on its exclusive assertion 'Quest XP is a table, NOT a formula'. The 69 rows are real (I counted 69 <exp>, distinct set 100/200/250/290/500/600/750/1000/2000/3000, and questdata.xml:214-216 = 290 and :411-413 = 200 are line-exact). But there is a second quest system the claim misses: proc-gen daily quests build their reward XML at RUNTIME. QuestGenerator.as emits 'rewardStr += "<exp>" + questReward + "</exp>";' at ~28 sites with questReward = (getXPLevelThreshhold(nodelvl+1) - getXPLevelThreshhold(nodelvl)) / ((nodelvl+1)*1.2) (QuestGenerator.as:839, 1001, 1228, 1465, 1644, 1839, 2105, 2266, 2417 …), and getXPLevelThreshhold is literally 'return expArray[level]' (StatsManager.as:1604-1606). WEB parity is present: §1t123s0§.as:878/1039/1283/1522 and §1t27s0§.as:317. And THE FRAME SETTLES IT — the only quest-XP number visible in either longplay is 473 (video B ~t=1:01:51 waypoint reward), which is NOT one of the 69 tabled values but IS exactly the formula at node level 7: (20900-16350)/(8*1.2) = 473.958 → int 473. I computed neighbours to rule out coincidence: nodelvl 5→527, 6→500, 7→473, 8→462, 9→458, 10→454, 11→423. THE FRAME WINS over the table-only reading. A port following this claim literally would ship the 61 authored quests' XP and silently drop the entire daily-quest faucet.

verdicts.reason: MAXRELOAD IS 192 (8*24), NOT 120. The survey cites §1t99s0§.as:55, but that constant (§1t12234s0§) has exactly two uses in the whole web bundle — §1t99s0§.as:266 and §1t122s0§.as:950, both assigning §1t4440s0§, a per-frame countdown decremented at :1246. It never reaches the meter. The real maxreload is §1t4415s0§ — the var compared in getDamage (:3272), zeroed in deductReloadBar (:3295), clamped in the refill (:3321) and passed to the UI as param2 (:256,:1208,:3169,:3325) — and it is assigned once, at :249, to 8*24 = 192 frames = 8.00 s. Line 249 sits inside §1t4443s0§ (declared :183), the 15-param twin of Android MCSPlayer.as:182 initPlayer (same arity, same order, param-for-param at :185-199 vs :184-198); the Android twin of line 249 is MCSPlayer.as:239 `this.maxreload = 5 * 24`. verdicts.reason: The android quote is verbatim (MCSPlayer.as:3029-3081) and the negative grep is honest - I reproduced it and '0.5 + 0.5 *', '1 + 0.5 *' and '0.005' all return zero hits across shs3_payload/scripts/. (1) v0.717 DOES carry the per-stance slash multipliers, in the same shape of switch, at §1t99s0§.as:3091-3146: LIGHT '* 1.4', BALANCED '* (1 + 0.2 * m * 0.1)', HEAVY '* (0.5 + 0.4 * m * 0.1)' with the same '< 100' floor, REVERSED '* 1.4', DUAL '* 1.0' floored 100. So parity is not merely unestablished - it is DISPROVED, and the desktop values are recovered. (2) The lane_impact's 'mastery is a 0-100 percentage here, not 0-9' is false: skills 1000/1001/1002 are Light/Balanced/Heavy Stance Mastery with exactly 10 <level> rows in BOTH tables (reference/extracted/skilldata.xml and reference/extracted/android/117_Mobile_SkillData.bin), and MCSPlayer.as:3166 gates canLaunch on 'lightMastery >= 3', only meaningful on a 1-10 scale. The android '* 0.01' coefficient is a rebalance, not a different stat domain. The instruction this claim sends to combat-core therefore points the wrong way: the ledger was off by one, not off by an order of magnitude.

new_findings.lane_impact: combat-core: the damage multipliers become CONTRACT from the shipped v0.717 client rather than a wiki reading. Light scales 0.54 -> 0.9 across mastery 1-10, Balanced 1.02 -> 1.2, Heavy/Dual/Reversed a flat 1.4 with no mastery term at all. The ceiling is mastery 10 (skilldata gives skills 1000/1001/1002 exactly ten levels), so every 'mastery-9' label in the ledger should read mastery-10. It also means Heavy is the only stance whose damage does NOT improve with mastery - a design fact absent from the board.

new_findings.text: The rebirth payout is Heavenly Gold, the real-money PayVault currency, not the coin economy - so a 'tenthGold' config key modelled as coins would be wrong even with the right number.
new_findings.quote: public static function getHeavenlyGold() : int { var hgold:int = getPlayerStats(STAT_HGOLD); if(usePlayerIO) { hgold += QueryManagerPIO.instance.getPayVaultCoins(); } return hgold; } ... QueryManagerPIO.instance.debitPayVaultCoins(deductgold, ...)
new_findings.ledger_text: film shows a **flat +25 gold** every rebirth, no 10th-rebirth tier.
new_findings.lane_impact: economy + rebirth-elements: rebirth is a premium-currency faucet, which is why the desktop anti-cheat tolerates 300 of it only once DAN >= 9 (§1t406s0§.as:1544) while capping coins separately (OverworldHUD.as:1338, STAT_GOLD > 10000). The ledger's film-derived '+25 gold' was reading the Heavenly Gold counter, not the coin counter. verdicts.reason: The z-order table is 23 layers on a human, not 27. MCSCharacter.as:120 declares `internal var partListLength:int = 22;` and the loop the surveyor quoted (:141) is `i <= this.partListLength`, so exactly 23 MovieClips (0-22) are allocated. PART_l_shoulder(23)/r_shoulder(24)/l_knee(25)/r_knee(26) are never allocated on a human and are read ONLY by MCSWolf.as:184,188,193,197, where they mean front/back legs, after MCSWolf.as:13 extends the list with `partListLength = 25`. The surveyor read :10-62 and :141-146 but skipped :120, 21 lines above the loop it quoted. A builder coding the claim's '27-entry z-ordered enum' for equipment builds four phantom layers. The rest of the claim I verified and it holds: nothing calls setChildIndex/swapChildren on the top-level partList (the six setChildIndex calls at :683,:706,:724,:755,:873,:885 reorder inside a part container), armor drives 7 parts and pants drives 5 (I counted the addChild(componentObject) sites myself), and the partType+art / partType+"0" contract at :581-607 is verbatim.

verdicts.reason: There are at least two icon-only art namespaces that are not paperdoll parts, in the same class the surveyor read. MCSItem.as:206 `this.displayItem = this.getMCSComponent("item",id);` with fallback `new item0()` at :209, and MCSItem.as:229 `this.getMCSComponent("acc",id);`. Neither "item" nor "acc" is a PART_* type; there is no MCSCharacter setter for either, and accessories are not even passed to initMCS (StatsManager.as:1765 passes 11 slots, ACCESSORY1/2 excluded). On top of that the Android bundle carries 11 named placeholder icon classes (ArmorDummyIcon, PantsDummyIcon, HatDummyIcon, MaskDummyIcon, GlovesDummyIcon, ShoesDummyIcon, WeaponDummyIcon, AccessoryDummyIcon, ConsumableDummyIcon, InvalidDummyIcon, AchievementDummyIcon). The frame proves the consequence: of the 7 inventory icons in the crop, five are a scroll, an onigiri x3, a black stone and two feathers - none can be a torso/pelvic/uparm stack. 'One art pipeline, not two; no icon-authoring pass is needed' is wrong.

verdicts.reason: The headline is true but the actionable conclusion is the exact mis-wiring it claims to prevent. ShopItem.as:27 `internal var borderType:String = "normal";` and :51-52 `this.borderType = itemRef.getShopItemType(); gotoAndStop(this.borderType + "_default");` - the border frame label IS the 4-value rarity enum returned by Item.getShopItemType() (normal|special|rare|unique, Item.as:382-405), across four states (:283,:287,:295,:299 = _selectedmouseover/_mouseover/_selected/_default), i.e. a 4 tiers x 4 states = 16 frame-label art contract. InventoryUI.as:1453 passes `clickedItem.getBorderType()` - the method is named for the border. And four lines above the tip the surveyor quoted, GameEngine.as:568 reads 'Tip: A blue border indicates that an item is rare.' So the border does track the rarity ladder; 'unique' is its top tier, not a flag beside it. Frame corroboration in the same crop: two purple borders (unique), the selected Branch tile is normal_selected (same tan border, darkened fill), four are normal_default.

The derivation half (unique-flag + modifier count, no rarity field) and the eight hexes are correct - it is the parity conclusion that is wrong.

verdicts.reason: The claim says the four-band floor 'lives in boss auto-scaling, not the generic defense pipeline' and is keyed to playerLVL. Both halves fail. Damage.as:149-172 is the GENERIC damage class carrying the identical ladder keyed on the ATTACKER: 'getMinDamage(): if(this.attackerlvl == 0) return this.damage; if(this.attackerlvl <= 10) return 1 + this.piercingDamage; if(this.attackerlvl <= 20) return this.attackerlvl / 8 + this.piercingDamage; if(this.attackerlvl <= 30) return this.attackerlvl / 6 + this.piercingDamage; return this.attackerlvl / 4 + this.piercingDamage;'. It is applied on the PLAYER's damage-taking path immediately after defense subtraction, MCSPlayer.as:3415-3419: 'damage -= this.getDefense(); if(damage < damageObj.getMinDamage()) { damage = damageObj.getMinDamage(); }' — and in 9 files total (EnemyClone, EnemyJiangSi, EnemyNianMonster, EnemyWolfAlpha, EnemyShield, EnemyZombie, EnemySpearElite, MCSPlayer x2). When an enemy hits the player the attacker IS the enemy, so above attacker level 30 the floor is EnemyLevel/4 — exactly the ledger bullet. EnemyPlayer.as:107-123 (the surveyor's cite) is real but is the player-attacking-a-boss MIRROR of the same ladder, used to size boss HP. The ledger's 'defense min-floor (EnemyLevel/4)' is CORRECT — incomplete (omits the three lower bands and the +piercingDamage term) but right in variable and right in shape. Acting on this claim would replace a right ledger line with a wrong one.
verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/Damage.as:149-172 and MCSPlayer.as:3415-3419 (grep: damageObj.getMinDamage() applied in 9 files)

verdicts.reason: The claim rests on `ls shs3_payload/scripts | grep -ci enemy|npc` -> 0, concluding the web v0.717 build has no gameplay code so parity is unestablished. That test cannot work: the web build is NAME-OBFUSCATED. 667 `§...§.as` classes exist there and they ARE the gameplay code. §1t68s0§.as IS the web NPC class — its setLevel is semantically identical to Android NPC.as:239-260 (factor = lvl/level, *0.9 at <=20, damage/defense/maxhp *= factor, xp = lvl*2+20, <=10 clamp to 1/1/1). Further exact parity: aiCounterMax = 24 at the SAME line 22; hit lockout = 12; Projectile GRAVITY:Number = 3 at the SAME line 8; ttlMax = 48 at the SAME line 22; atan(velY/velX)*57.2727+180. Absence of the NAME is not absence of the CODE. Parity is DEMONSTRATED, which strikes cap-reason (1) — the stated dominant residual risk — from the score rationale.
verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/§1t68s0§.as:258-279 (setLevel), :22 (=24), :483 (=12); §1t128s0§.as:8 (GRAVITY=3), :22 (ttlMax=48); find shs3_payload -name '*§*.as' | wc -l -> 667

verdicts.reason: Android side reproduces verbatim (0.866 launch factor, 60px muzzle, ±4 jitter via Math.random()*8-4, GRAVITY=3, ttlMax=48, level-gated knockdown >50 1-in-2 / >20 1-in-3 / >10 1-in-4). But the claim asserts a FIXED GRAVITY=3 solve, and that is false for the web v0.717 build — the 1:1 target the reference videos show. The web archer computes the knockdown roll FIRST and then OVERRIDES gravity to 1.5 for that shot: `var _loc6_:Number = §1t128s0§.§1t12543s0§; if(_loc1_) { _loc6_ = 1.5; }`, feeding _loc6_ into both the velA term and the 0.5*g*t*t term. Android EnemyArcher.as:277 has no such branch. Knockdown arrows fly a flatter, faster arc than the claim describes.
verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/§1t4542s0§.as:287-299 vs reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/EnemyArcher.as:271-302

Gold is NOT player-exclusive (all Friendly* share it), and elites/guardians/duelists are WHITE, not red. 0x990000 is reserved for opposing-SIDE duelists/bosses. new_findings.text: Enemy level scaling is not one formula but twelve: NPC.setLevel is overridden by eleven subclasses, EnemyOgre's override is EMPTY (ogres never level-scale), EnemyPlayer / EnemyElite / EnemyKanjiGuardian drop both the x0.9 sub-21 factor and the 1/1/1 clamp and pay xp = lvl*5 + 45, and the elite/boss variants additionally run a player-relative autobalance (hitsToKillBoss = 8 or 10 or 13 + lvldiff, hitsToKillPlayer = 16 - lvldiff) that rewrites minDamage and maxhp against the live player's stats.

verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/Obj_NPCAggro.as:34-37,62,73-80 + NPCManager.as:671,879,895,910,934; frame reference/frames/zFtCaTO0_1M/seg-10/frames/frame_0013.jpg reproduced at the stated crop (340,320)->(900,480) LANCZOS x3 AND at x2 full-frame
verdicts.reason: Two failures. (a) The stated crop does not contain two of its own listed observations: I reproduced (340,320)->(900,480) x3 exactly and it holds only the two bandits and the red BANDIT (4) plates. The gold GUEST label is at x~205 (left of x0=340) and TERRITORY (22,51)/SECTOR (1,2) is at y~272-295 (above y0=320). Both are true of the FRAME (I confirmed at x2 full) but not of the CROP, and under this lens the crop is the cite. (b) The load-bearing half is refuted by code: there is no frame-vs-doc conflict to resolve. Obj_NPCAggro.as:34-37 reads the level from the room-object property string (this.lvl = strArray[1]); :73-80 uses it ONLY as a display string (hideHealthBar(); setDisplayName(npcname + " (" + lvl + ")", 10027008)); :62 spawns via NPCManager.createRoomNPC(npcid,posX,posY,doChase), whose signature at NPCManager.as:671 has NO lvl parameter and never calls setLevel(). setLevel() has exactly four call sites (NPCManager.as:879,895,910,934), all wave/quest spawns. So the (4) is a cosmetic per-placement override, the bandit keeps npcdata's lvl 10 / hp 15, and the <=10 clamp never fires. 'A real on-screen HP of 1' is unproven, and invoking THE FRAME WINS where the source explicitly authors the value manufactures a conflict in order to resolve it. SURVIVES: the red all-caps parenthesised-level plate and the gold GUEST are both real (verified at x2 full-frame), and the colour is now code-held as 10027008 = 0x990000.

verdicts.own_cite: reference/extracted/android/99_MCSCharacter_HumanAnimationData.bin re-parsed by me (158 <anim>), plus my own sum over all 18 *AnimationData.bin = 471
verdicts.reason: Every DURATION is exact - I re-derived them (heavyhorizontalslash_parta 6 / _partb 9 l="1" / _partc 7, balanced 4/9/7, katanaattack 10, stabattack 14, downstab 15, ninjaslash 8, pullbackarrow 9, pullbackarrow_full 15, firearrow 1, arrownormalpose 22) and the 471 total matches. The RULE is wrong. 'Every stance attack ships as three named parts' is false and is contradicted by the claim's own quote field, which contains lighthorizontalslash:3 - a single anim with no parts. My parse: only 16 anim families use _part decomposition (48 part-anims), and the count is not uniformly three - balancedjumpslash and heavyjumpslash have 5, punchcombo 4, jutsu_ground/jutsu_punch/jutsu_blow/stomp/punchground 2. Many attacks have no decomposition at all: lighthorizontalslash, downstab(15), stabattack(14), katanaattack(10), ninjaslash(8), holdshieldstabattack(10), downstab_up(10). A port built on 'every stance attack = parta/partb/partc' invents a three-phase light slash and three-phase katana/stab attacks the source does not have. The underlying finding (telegraph/active/recovery timing IS authored per-frame; blocker (3)'s first half is dead) stands.

verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/NPCManager.as:516-636 (I counted the case labels and extracted every `new X` myself) + NPCManager.as:671 createRoomNPC
verdicts.reason: Count overstated. I counted 38 case labels but only 34 DISTINCT classes - EnemyPlayer appears 3x, EnemyWolf 2x, EnemySpearElite 2x. Of the 34, three are Friendly*, so it is 31 Enemy* + 3 Friendly*, not the claimed '34 named Enemy* classes plus 3 Friendly*' (=37). The score rationale's '38 behaviour classes are unwritten work' is likewise 34. Also missed: the 38-case switch is not the only dispatch. NPCManager.as:671 createRoomNPC() - the path every overworld enemy takes - runs an independent if/else chain on xml.ai (ai==8 -> EnemyWolf, ai==11||16 -> EnemyWolfAlpha, ai==12 -> ...). A recreation modelling only the switch misses the overworld branch. The core structural point - <ai> indexes a behaviour class rather than a difficulty tier, so the shipped 3-tier AI_TIERS is the wrong SHAPE - holds and is the most valuable claim in the unit.

verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/NPC.as:462 and :296-299, plus my own grep of every canHit() call site -> NPCManager.as:1222,1263,1325,1414,1434,1454,1494,1513,1534,1564,1579
verdicts.reason: The number is right (gotHitCounter = 12 at NPC.as:462) and the negative half is right - I confirmed no stagger/flinch/gothit anim among the 158 human names, only the launch/knockdown chain (gotlaunchedupwards_parta/b/c 4/9/7, gotlauncheddowned 18, downedup 4, downedup2 25, deathdowned 7). But 'hit-lockout' is the wrong mechanic. Every one of the eleven canHit() call sites is in NPCManager's HIT-DETECTION, in the form !enemy.isDead() && enemy.canHit() && enemy.testHit(thing). gotHitCounter gates whether the enemy CAN BE HIT - 12 frames of damage immunity (i-frames). It does not stop the enemy acting. A porter reading 'hit-lockout' implements an action lock, a real behavioural divergence. The '/ i-frames' hedge in lane_impact is the correct reading; the claim text is not. The PARTIAL verdict and the call for frame-side confirmation are honest and correct.

verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/EnemyArcher.as:271-302 read verbatim + Projectile.as:8 (GRAVITY=3) and :22 (ttlMax=48) + ArrowProjectile.as:48-60
verdicts.reason: The solve, the +/-4 scatter, GRAVITY=3, ttlMax=48 and the knockdown gate (>50 1-in-2, >20 1-in-3, >10 1-in-4, else never) are all verbatim-correct; I read every one. But 'a fixed 30 degree launch (0.866 = cos30)' is wrong. 0.866 only scales the HORIZONTAL speed: velA = sqrt(g*dx/0.866), velXa = 0.866*velA = sqrt(0.866*g*dx). The vertical component is then SOLVED from the ballistic constraint to pass through the target (velYa = (targetY-fireY-0.5*g*t*t)/t), so the true launch angle atan(velYa/velXa) varies with range and height difference. Firing at a literal 30 degrees reproduces neither the trajectory nor the hit rate. Minor: rotation = atan(velY/velX)*57.2727+180 sits inside if(breakable) at ArrowProjectile.as:53, not unconditionally as presented.

new_findings.text: AP==0 in adventure mode does not kill or retreat the player — it swaps the idle animation to "tired"; outside adventure mode the same pose fires at HP <= maxhp/4.
new_findings.lane_impact: L1 world-exploration and L6 art-anim: CORRECTS the world-exploration journal's own lane_impact on claim ap-regen-and-cap, which reads this line as "a death/retreat condition". It is an idle-pose selector. grep for `STAT_AP) == 0` across all 559 android classes returns this single line — there is no AP-death rule anywhere. The portable rule is: adventure-mode idle has two poses (tired / idle_sheathed) gated on AP==0, and duel-mode idle has two poses gated on HP <= 25%. That is a real L6 animation-state finding the ledger does not carry.

new_findings.text: The war tick the ledger names as a consumer of the "day" length runs on a 3600-second clock, and duel tokens on a 120-second clock, so blocker ③'s single-day-clock premise fails on five independent clocks, not three.
new_findings.quote_note: three sibling constants on consecutive declarations
new_findings.ledger_text: ③ real-world **"day" length** (governs expiry, farming, AP regen, war tick).
new_findings.lane_impact: L1 world-exploration and L11 meta-social: strengthens and corrects the journal's day-length-is-three-clocks claim. The ledger's ③ explicitly lists the "war tick" as governed by the day length; WARMOVEINTERVAL=3600 kills that outright — the war moves hourly. Full clock inventory: AP 60 s, duel tokens 120 s, war move 3600 s, crops 900/3600/21600/43200 s (+900 s grace), quest repeat + daily streak 86400 s. Five independent real-time clocks, all measured in raw seconds off QueryManager.getServerTime(). The save schema corroborates: slots 100/101/102 are nextAPUpdate / nextDTUpdate / nextWarTurn, three separate persisted timestamps.

new_findings.text: A Rock deposit (oreType 1) is an unlimited faucet — the despawn is guarded on oreType != 1, so it can be mined for 2 AP indefinitely, unlike every other ore which is added to the dead list on first success.
new_findings.lane_impact: L1 world-exploration and L2 economy: refines the journal's "'Respawn' is not a timer" line, which is right but incomplete. Combined with the 50% downgrade-to-Rock rule at Obj_OreDeposit.as:70, the real loop is: any non-Coal deposit has a 50% chance of yielding item 20059 ("Unusable rocks") AND staying on the map, so the node is farmable until the player rolls the real ore. That is an economy sink/faucet the ledger has no line for.

new_findings.text: Town levels are frozen for 19 territories, not the 12 explicitly listed ids — isNoChangeTown also returns true for every territory whose level is below LEVELSTART+5.
new_findings.lane_impact: L1 world-exploration and L11 meta-social: extends the journal's prosperity-thresholds claim, which lists only the 12 hard-coded ids. The real rule is a radius: any territory with level < 8, i.e. Manhattan distance <= 4 from (341,341). I counted these over the land mask myself — 19 territories (L3x1 + L4x2 + L5x4 + L6x5 + L7x7). So the starting region is a fixed, non-warrable tutorial zone by construction, and only the 716 outer territories have dynamic prosperity.

new_findings.lane_impact: L1 world-exploration: a porting hazard against world-exploration/place-name-reproduced-from-payload, logged as a lead because it rests on constant-pool adjacency rather than a quoted line of code. Evidence for: NameGenerator.as:136-144 hardcodes exactly two exceptions ('Ibamaya' for territoryID 1405272, 'Gokura' for 1524045), neither of which appears in 89_NameGenerator_PlaceNames.bin; the WEB payload's constant pool carries three capitalised place names adjacently at payload.xml:119264-119266 -- Ibamaya, Gokura, Iwakuni -- immediately after the nameending array and the 'replace' token used only by the name functions; and grep -rn Iwakuni over all 559 android classes returns 0 files. Evidence against my own hypothesis: 'Iwakuni' IS a normal row of the PlaceNames blob, sitting in a run of real Japanese cities (Hofu / Iwakuni / Kudamatsu / Mine / Nagato), so its presence in the blob is innocent -- but a blob row does not need to be an AS3 string constant. Separately confirmed and NOT in doubt: the web pool's namestarting and nameending runs match the android arrays in order and content with exactly the two absences a deduplicating pool predicts (Kiyo once instead of twice; 'i' and 'no' deduped), so the generator TABLES are cross-build consistent. Closing this needs a web-side NameGenerator decompile, which the repo does not hold.

verdicts.reason: 'EACH black shutter takes 17 frames' is wrong. TRANSITION_BLACKOPEN (ScreenTransition.as:93-108) has NO counter gate - unlike BLACKCLOSE it calls doAction() the instant blackup.y <= -240. Simulated: OPEN completes at frame 16 (y lands on exactly -240.0) = 666.7 ms, not 708. The derivation is also wrong: speed is applied BEFORE it increments, so displacement after n frames is n(n-1), not the quoted (n-2)(n-1); n=16 gives 240 exactly, so the shutter is physically shut at frame 16 and the counter>=17 gate holds it one EXTRA frame - that gate is not 'why' the arithmetic lands on 240. CLOSE=17f/708.3ms survives. WHITE=24f survives only because startOpenWhite's SOLE caller (Overworld.as:377) passes ACTION_REFRESHROOMONOPEN, whose case re-sets transitioning=true after the counter==2 doAction() - otherwise the fade freezes at alpha 0.917; the surveyor never checked that. 'EXACTLY 24' is also not exact: alpha -= 1/24 from 1.0 needs 25 iterations under IEEE doubles and only lands on 24 if Flash stores alpha as float32. Finally the 24 fps was never cited; it is not Mobile.as:117 (a frameRate==0 fallback) but the SWF headers, which I parsed.
verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/ScreenTransition.as:71-123,143-146,159-162 + Overworld.as:377 + python simulation ('CLOSE done at frame 17' / 'OPEN done at frame 16 y -240.0' / 'WHITE done at frame 25') + SWF header parse of reference/decrypted/shs3_android_payload_decoded.swf (800x480 @ 24.0 fps) and shs3_payload_decoded.swf (800x690 @ 24.0 fps)

new_findings.text: The two black shutters are NOT symmetric: the closing shutter runs 17 frames (708 ms) because of an explicit counter gate, but the opening shutter has no gate and completes in 16 frames (667 ms).
new_findings.quote: `else if(this.transitionType == TRANSITION_BLACKOPEN){ this.blackup.y -= this.blackMovtSpeed; this.blackdown.y += this.blackMovtSpeed; this.blackMovtSpeed += 2; if(this.blackup.y <= -240){ this.blackup.y = -240; this.blackdown.y = 480; ... this.doAction(); } }` - no `counter` test anywhere in the branch. From startOpen (`blackup.y = 0; blackMovtSpeed = 0; counter = 0;`) displacement after n frames is n(n-1), so n=16 gives exactly 240 and the branch fires at frame 16. Simulation output: 'OPEN done at frame 16 y -240.0' vs 'CLOSE done at frame 17'.
new_findings.lane_impact: ui-hud lane: corrects this pass's claim ui-hud/transition-durations-exact, which asserts 17 frames for both shutters. Also invalidates the stated derivation (n-2)(n-1); the correct displacement law is n(n-1).

verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/ScreenTransition.as:95-106 (BLACKOPEN branch) and :80-89, :111, :118, :143-146, :173; SWF header of reference/decrypted/shs3_payload_decoded.swf and shs3_android_payload_decoded.swf parsed first-hand
verdicts.reason: 'each black shutter takes 17 frames (708 ms)' is wrong for the OPEN shutter. The BLACKOPEN branch has NO counter gate -- :98 `if(this.blackup.y <= -240)` falls straight through to :106 `this.doAction();`. I simulated the exact integer loop: since speed is applied before it increments, displacement after n frames is n(n-1), not the claim's (n-2)(n-1); n(n-1)=240 at n=16. So the open shutter completes in 16 frames / 667 ms. The stated derivation is also fabricated: at frame 17 displacement is 272, not 240, and the close takes 17 frames only because the shutter sits shut one extra frame waiting on the :87 `counter >= 17` gate -- right answer, invented reason. White fade: with white.alpha=1 (:173) and `alpha -= 1/24` (:111), plain IEEE-754 doubles need 25 iterations (residual after 24 is ~1.1e-16 > 0); 24 holds only under Flash's 8.8 alpha quantisation, which the claim does not state. And :118 `if(this.counter == 2) doAction();` means the gameplay handoff is 2 frames. Its lane_impact 'third independent confirmation of the 480-px stage height' is cross-build: I parsed the SWF rects myself -- web payload is 800x690, android is 800x480. 24 fps is confirmed for both.

new_findings.text: The black screen-shutter is asymmetric: closing takes 17 frames (708 ms) but opening takes 16 frames (667 ms), because only the close path is counter-gated.
new_findings.cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/ScreenTransition.as:80-89 vs :95-106; 24.0 fps from the SWF headers of reference/decrypted/shs3_payload_decoded.swf and shs3_android_payload_decoded.swf
new_findings.quote: Close: `if(this.blackup.y >= 0){ ... if(this.counter >= 17){ this.doAction(); } }` (:83-89). Open: `if(this.blackup.y <= -240){ ... this.doAction(); }` (:98-106) — no counter test. Speed is applied before it increments (:80-82), so displacement after n frames is n(n-1), which equals 240 at n=16; the open path therefore fires at frame 16 and the close path holds one extra frame for the gate.

verdicts.reason: Two failures. (a) THE ARITHMETIC IS WRONG. I reproduced the measurement exactly - thr 25/40/60 all give cols 52..1867, w 1816, aspect 1.6814814814814816, with hard edges (col means 1.1 -> 39.7 -> 83.8 at cols 51-53, and 82.9 -> 68.3 -> 29.1 -> 2.0 at cols 1864-1867). The claim asserts 'aspect 1.6815 = 800x480'. It is not: 800/480 = 1.666667, so the measurement is 0.89% off, and the surveyor printed both numbers side by side and called them equal. Run the client's own letterbox math for 1920x1080: newScale = 1080/480 = 2.25, surface = 800*2.25 = 1800 px, offsetX = (1920-1800)/2 = 60, i.e. cols 60..1859. The frame shows 52..1867 - 16 px wider. The frame is consistent with 800x480 to ~1%, not equal to it, and any rebuild mapping cols 52..1867 onto 0..800 inherits that error. (b) 'THE FRAME WINS over the SWF document rect' is a MANUFACTURED CONFLICT. The surveyor cited GameEngine.as's resizeHandler but skipped the lines inside it that already answer the question: :271 `var originalHeightWithBar:int = 690;` :273 `var originalWithBarAspectRatio:Number = originalWidth / originalHeightWithBar;` :275 `if(newAspectRatio <= originalWithBarAspectRatio)` :278 `originalHeight = originalHeightWithBar;` :279 `StatsManager.stageShowingFriendBar = true;`. The payload itself reconciles 690 as the 800x690 friend-bar layout mode, entered when window aspect <= 800/690 = 1.1594. There was never a doc-vs-frame disagreement for the standing invariant to arbitrate; invoking it here on a citation that omits the answering lines is exactly the over-claim this lens hunts. The conclusion (design canvas is 800x480) survives; the route and the stated equality do not.

new_findings.text: The d-equals-frame-count invariant holds across ALL 19 web animdata blobs (487/487 anims, zero mismatches), but only under a robust parse: ~100 <anim> tags carry an extra attribute after d, so a strict regex silently drops them and manufactures phantom hold frames.

new_findings.quote: robust parse: total anims parsed 487, mismatches d != number-of-<f> : 0. Strict parse drops 38 of the 158 anims in 108_1t4635s0.bin (both `walk` d=20 and `light_run` d=9 are missed) and reports ~96 false mismatches such as ogre_swingdownhit d=5 vs 3 frames.
new_findings.lane_impact: art-anim-audio-feel: strengthens art-anim-audio-feel/24fps-keyframe-stream from a 2-blob sample to a proven universal across all 487 authored animations - the data genuinely holds no hold frames anywhere, and every latch is code-added by AnimData's duration tails. Also a standing measurement warning for any lane re-deriving animation counts or durations from the bindata XML: parse `<anim\b[^>]*>`, never `<anim i=".." d="..">`, or you lose the looping animations and invent hold frames that are not there.

new_findings.quote: light_stance frame0 node ids: ['19','16','15','14','13','12','11','10','9','7','6','5','4','2','1','0','20','18','3'] COUNT = 19  ·  MCSCharacter.as: 'public static var PART_l_hand:int = 0;' ... 'public static var PART_r_knee:* = 26;' (27 constants)
new_findings.lane_impact: art-anim-audio-feel (L6): the skeleton spec for the recreation. A 21-joint rig will not map onto the shipped keyframe data; build 19 keyed nodes for stances, 20 for the human set, and reserve the 27-slot part table for equipment/props.

new_findings.text: The 690-px stage height is not container chrome: it is originalHeightWithBar, a viewport-driven in-game friend panel the engine lays out itself, and the web build shipped the 690 stage while the Android build shipped the 480 one.
new_findings.quote: GameEngine.as:271 `var originalHeightWithBar:int = 690;`  ·  :277-283 `if(newAspectRatio <= originalWithBarAspectRatio) { originalAspectRatio = originalWithBarAspectRatio; originalHeight = originalHeightWithBar; StatsManager.stageShowingFriendBar = true; if(OverworldHUD.instance != null) { OverworldHUD.instance.friendpanel.init(); } }`  ·  headers I decoded: shs3_payload_decoded.swf rect 800.0 x 690.0 · shs3_android_payload_decoded.swf rect 800.0 x 480.0
new_findings.ledger_text: **Aspect-ratio truth** — native canvas is **800×480 (5:3)**, so HUD x-fractions measured off 16:9 video may be pillarbox-wrong.
new_findings.lane_impact: ui-hud and meta-social, not art: the ledger's aspect-ratio unknown resolves to a TWO-MODE layout — 800x480 with the friend bar off (wide viewports, which is what both longplays record) and 800x690 with a game-drawn friendpanel on (narrow viewports). Neither ui-hud nor meta-social holds a friend panel. Also retires the false frame-vs-doc conflict in art-anim-audio-feel/aspect-ratio-frame-wins.

new_findings.text: The 24 Hz animation clock is provable on the web v0.717 build itself, not only via the Android client or the Kongregate loader shell.
new_findings.cite: SWF header of reference/decrypted/shs3_payload_decoded.swf, decoded and parsed by me
new_findings.quote: reference/decrypted/shs3_payload_decoded.swf: sig=CWS v17 len=11,892,061 rect_px=800.0 x 690.0 framerate=24.0 frames=6
new_findings.lane_impact: art-anim-audio-feel: replaces the two weaker cites behind the 24 fps claim. The survey used shs3.swf (the loader shell — 2 frames, DoABC + SymbolClass, no game content) and Mobile.as:117 (Android). This one is the web payload's own header, so the clock carries no Android caveat and the PARTIAL on 24fps-keyframe-stream can be re-argued upward.

new_findings.text: The "150% DAMAGE" line in the duel HUD is the timed BUFF_ATTACK consumable readout, not the stance modifier — the string is a literal in the client.
new_findings.cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/OverworldHUD.as:1388-1428 (updateBuff); docs/gauntlet/L0/index/strings.json id 4132; corroborated in reference/frames/duel_dense/Nr4fQstqHDM_432.0.png crop (52,900)-(700,1080) x3

new_findings.lane_impact: ui-hud gains a required buff-text slot (OverworldHUD.bufftext, htmlText, hidden when duration <= 0 or the stats button is hidden). Closes the "un-reconciled" caution the surveyor left on art-anim-audio-feel/hit-reaction-12-ticks, and closes it against the surveyor's own guess.

new_findings.text: The stance rock-paper-scissors multiplier is x1.2, not x1.5, and a stance-advantage hit also recolours the damage popup to white.
new_findings.quote: `if(this.stance == LIGHT_STANCE && enemyStance == BALANCED_STANCE || this.stance == BALANCED_STANCE && enemyStance == HEAVY_STANCE || this.stance == HEAVY_STANCE && enemyStance == LIGHT_STANCE) { damage *= 1.2; if(this.controlledBy != 0) { damagetextcol = 16777215; } }`
new_findings.lane_impact: combat-core: the damage pipeline in one order — stance triangle x1.2, then subtract defense, then clamp to damageObj.getMinDamage(), then behead x1.5, then add the four elemental damages. Three distinct multipliers exist (stance 1.2, behead 1.5, BUFF_ATTACK 150%) and the ledger conflates none of them because it holds none of them.

verdicts.own_cite: reference/videos/Nr4fQstqHDM.mp4 (ffprobe: r_frame_rate=60/1, 1920x1080, 237047 frames) — 150 consecutive frames extracted at t=428s; and reference/videos/zFtCaTO0_1M.mp4 (r_frame_rate=60/1) — 120 frames at t=900s. Luma MAE on play-area crop [400:1000, 500:1500].
verdicts.reason: THE FRAME WINS, and I say so out loud. The claim's stated reason for grading PARTIAL is factually false: it says 'no frame can arbitrate the visible cadence: the dense stills sample at 0.1 s (10 Hz)'. reference/frames/duel_dense/ is a pre-extracted SUBSET; the primary reference is 1080p60 video and it arbitrates decisively. My inter-frame MAE on Nr4fQstqHDM @428s: 0.42 5.94 0.05 0.02 0.02 5.29 0.02 0.02 0.03 4.95 0.00 0.03 0.00 3.17 ... — mean MAE by index mod 4 = [0.061, 3.076, 0.026, 0.069]. On the SECOND, independent longplay zFtCaTO0_1M @900s: mod 4 = [0.003, 0.040, 6.438, 0.078]. Unique content lands on exactly every 4th frame of 60, phase-locked over 150 frames, in two separate captures. 60/4 = 15 Hz. A 24 Hz game in a 60 fps capture would beat at an irregular 2/3/2/3 cadence; neither video shows that, and there is no 24 Hz signature anywhere. This independently reproduces docs/research/SHSD_MASTER_REFERENCE.md:892 and docs/DIVERGENCES.md:333. So REBUILD_READINESS.md:239's '15fps pose latch' is frame-measured and STANDS; the claim's lane_impact ('the headline Ready bullet's model is wrong') is itself the wrong call — this is precisely the lens-3 failure, overturning a frame-backed ledger line from a byte inference while asserting frames cannot decide. SURVIVING: @d == count(<f>) is TRUE — my attribute-tolerant regex over all 19 web animdata blobs gives 0/487 mismatches; AnimData.as:15/:41 duration tails and MCSCharacter.as:1315/:1334 latch-on-overrun are verbatim correct; and SWF headers really do declare 24.0 fps (I parsed shs3.swf, shs3_payload_decoded.swf, shs3_android_payload_decoded.swf). The honest statement is 'the SWF stage declares 24 Hz; the shipped game visibly steps poses at 15 Hz'. Weak sub-cite too: Mobile.as:117 sits inside handleMobileActivate guarded by if(frameRate == 0) — an AIR resume-from-background handler in the Android build, not the web clock.

verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/EnemyShield.as:338 `gotHitCounter = 24;`; MCSPlayer.as:1457 `gotHitCounter = 24;`, :1461 `gotHitCounter = 84;`, :1764 `gotHitCounter = 26;`, :1768 `gotHitCounter = 16;`
verdicts.reason: 'A single uniform 12-tick window ... set identically in every enemy class and in MCSPlayer' is false, and MCSPlayer is itself the counterexample. gotHitCounter takes at least five values: 12 (default, 23 sites), 16 (recovery after SKILL_DEADLYCLEAVE_STATE, MCSPlayer.as:1768), 24 (shield/prop block, EnemyShield.as:338; DOWNSTAB in redfreeze, MCSPlayer.as:1457), 26 (after SKILL_THOUSANDSTABS_STATE, :1764), 84 (local player in REDFREEZE_STATE, :1461). This kills the lane_impact outright: 'the authored 7/12/16-frame tint ladder is a recreation invention — the original's single number is 12' — the original's set CONTAINS both 12 and 16, so two of the recreation's three rungs are vindicated, not invented. What holds: MCSPlayer.as:3689-3692 PART_hat/PART_head/PART_neck -> behead = true, :3716 damage *= 1.5, :3719 gotHitCounter = 12 are all verbatim correct, and the x1.5 body-part multiplier is a real find. Their own 'CAUTION, un-reconciled' was answerable from the index they were handed: docs/gauntlet/L0/index/strings.json entry 4132 = 'Eat this potato to get the 150% Damage buff.' — the HUD's '150% DAMAGE' is a consumable buff, NOT the stance modifier (which is damage *= 1.2 in the same function).

verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/GameEngine.as:271 `var originalHeightWithBar:int = 690;`, :275-281 `if(newAspectRatio <= originalWithBarAspectRatio){ originalHeight = originalHeightWithBar; StatsManager.stageShowingFriendBar = true; OverworldHUD.instance.friendpanel.init(); }`; plus my own SWF header parse of reference/decrypted/shs3_android_payload_decoded.swf (rect 16000x9600 twips = 800x480) and my own re-measure of reference/frames/duel_dense/Nr4fQstqHDM_432.0.png
verdicts.reason: The 800x480 CONCLUSION is correct and survives — three things around it are not. (1) There is no frame-vs-byte conflict for the frame to arbitrate: the payload explains its own 690 rect. 690 is originalHeightWithBar = the 480 play area PLUS a named in-game friend panel with its own class (OverworldHUD.instance.friendpanel), switched on conditionally when window aspect <= 800/690. 'Container chrome, not play area' mischaracterises it, and invoking 'THE FRAME WINS over the SWF document rect — I say so explicitly' for a self-consistent payload is precedence theatre. (2) overturns_ledger:true is wrong. REBUILD_READINESS.md:117 already says 'native canvas is 800x480 (5:3)' and :171 repeats it. The claim CONFIRMS the ledger and closes its open question ('are x-fractions pillarbox-wrong?') — a promotion, not an overturn; scoring it as an overturn inflates the unit. (3) The arithmetic is presented as an equality it is not: I reproduced their measurement exactly (thr 25/40/60 -> cols 52..1867, w=1816, aspect 1.6815) but 800/480 = 1.6667, a 0.9% gap (~16 px at 1080 tall). Finally, the direct byte answer they missed: the Android payload SWF's own document rect IS literally 800x480, while shs3.swf and shs3_payload_decoded.swf are 800x690 — i.e. the web containers carry the friend bar and the mobile one does not.

verdicts.own_cite: my own recursive PlaceObject3 parse (descending into every DefineSprite) of reference/extracted/android/115_Mobile_SHS3Resource.bin (key 104), 124_Mobile_ImageResource.bin (key 109), 120_Mobile_BGResource.bin (key 103), reference/decrypted/shs3_payload_decoded.swf and shs3_android_payload_decoded.swf; plus reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/ColorCode.as:1-10 imports
verdicts.reason: HEADLINE HOLDS AND I PROVED IT HARDER. The survey rested on an ActionScript grep, which cannot see blend modes authored on the timeline. I parsed every PlaceObject3 tag in all three decoded art containers and both decoded payloads: 12 + 1473 + 54 + 304 + 248 = 2,091 PlaceObject3 tags, ZERO blend-mode fields. Blocker 3 is closed by bytes, not inference. BUT THE TAIL OF THE CLAIM IS FALSE: 'the entire compositing vocabulary is one class using ColorTransform, BlurFilter and a luma ColorMatrixFilter' is contradicted by the same parse — the shipped art is full of timeline-authored filters ColorCode.as never constructs: Glow x1469 + Blur x4 in ImageResource, Blur x29 in BGResource, Glow x8 in SHS3Resource, Glow x152 + Blur x41 + DropShadow x2 in the web payload. ColorCode.as imports only BlurFilter and ColorMatrixFilter and never builds a GlowFilter or DropShadowFilter. A recreation built from the claim as written would omit glow entirely — and glow is visible in-frame on the yellow nameplate and HUD text. Not marked refuted because the blocker-closing negative is true and now byte-proven; the vocabulary sentence needs correcting in the journal.

verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/StageManager.as:903 `if(redFreezeCounter == 24 * 5)`, :916 `else if(redFreezeCounter == 24 && ...getAnim() != MCSActor.SHEATHESWORDCHIBURI || redFreezeCounter == 0)`, :926 `else if(redFreezeCounter == 24 * 3)`, :1096 `redFreezeCounter = 24 * 3 + 6;`, :1101 `redFreezeCounter = 24 * 6;`
verdicts.reason: All five line cites are exact and the SHEATHESWORDCHIBURI gate is real. Two corrections. (a) :1101 is the ELSE of the ACTION_HARVEST branch, so 24*6 is set on BOTH win and loss — it is not a win-specific value. (b) On a win the freeze normally ENDS at counter == 24 (:916), i.e. after 120 ticks; the full 144 runs only while the blood-flick sheathe is still playing. So '24*6 ticks (6.0 s)' is the ceiling, not the norm — the typical kill-beat is 120 ticks. Separately, every seconds figure here inherits the contested 24 Hz clock (see my fatal verdict on 24fps-keyframe-stream): carry the tick counts, label the seconds.

verdicts.reason: Three errors. (1) '690 is container chrome, not play area' is WRONG. GameEngine.as resizeHandler names it: ':271 var originalHeightWithBar:int = 690;' and when the window aspect <= 800/690 it does ':278 originalHeight = originalHeightWithBar; :279 StatsManager.stageShowingFriendBar = true;' and ':282 OverworldHUD.instance.friendpanel.init();'. The extra 210 px is the game's own IN-GAME FRIEND PANEL, a named second layout mode with its own state flag - a whole UI surface ui-hud does not know about. (2) 'THE FRAME WINS over the SWF document rect' is a FALSE CONFLICT. Both numbers are in the code with an explicit branch between them; the videos read 5:3 because they were captured in FULLSCREEN, where GameEngine.as:190 sets fullScreenSourceRect = new Rectangle(0,0,800*newScale,480*newScale) and drops the bar. Nothing was arbitrated. (3) The quoted letterbox formula is presented as unconditional but is the ELSE branch - 'if(originalAspectRatio >= newAspectRatio)' fits WIDTH with offsetX=0 and offsetY centred. And 'aspect 1.6815 = 800x480' is loose: 5:3 at 1080 height is 1800 px, not 1816; I reproduced 1816 on Nr4fQstqHDM_432.0.png but the OTHER longplay gives cols 55..1861 = 1807 wide, aspect 1.67315, so 1816 is a property of that upload, not the game. The surviving true part - visible surface is ~5:3, decisively not 800x690 (1.159) - is all that was needed.

result.score_rationale:
Re-score of the two systems this source owns.

skills-meters: ledger 33/100 -> 78/100. Four of its five blockers are dead on A2 evidence (① all 182 chi/cooldown rows verbatim; ② Shunpo's effect + gate + cost; ③ Focus = the reload meter, with max/fill/switch-cost all sourced; ④ the exact SPD->cooldown formula). Blocker ⑤ (crit proc rule) survives untouched, and one new open question appeared (the mastery domain in the reach formula), so this is not a 90+. The confidence is unusually high for a dead game because the payload's numbers reproduce the web longplay's on-screen cooldowns to the hundredth of a second at SPD=5 — three independent hits — and the android and web skilldata files are byte-identical (sha1 match). What remains for L2 is a transcription loop, not research.

rebirth-elements: ledger 30/100 -> 62/100. Blocker ① ('names only') is dead — all 24 elemental skills carry chi, cooldown and damage-as-%-of-element-ATK. Blocker ② is half-dead (ATK side sourced, DEF side not). The unlock gate is corrected from a rebirth count to a stat threshold (10/30/60), and Dragon Dance turns out to be 8 steps, not 4, and player-teachable. Blockers ③ (Dan-rank titles), ④'s input half, and ⑤ (the element-picker UI, never filmed) all survive, which caps this well below skills-meters.

Weighted across the 12 systems I cannot score — I only surveyed one source — so treat 78 as the skills-meters figure, not a board average.

No new_score returned — this is a SOURCE sweep, not a system sweep. But the board should note: enemies-ai's 34/100 is not a conservative floor, it is wrong. Four of its five listed blockers are wholly or half closed by one unread 228 KB file. Blocker ① (level→stat formula, "absent, not just inferred") is closed EXACTLY — a closed form reproduces 225/225 rows with zero violations. Blocker ② (per-enemy HP) is closed for 403/495 NPCs including every named boss. Blocker ④ (aggro/spawn) is half closed (34-profile AI assignment table held; behaviour bodies still in AS3). The moveset/"notes only" framing is closed by 647 authored skill rows. meta-social 31 also moves: the clan-war unit roster, level ladder and per-clan livery are fully held even though the server sim is not. items-equipment's "9-slot paperdoll" is a miscount — 10 wearable + 12 render slots.

claims.text: Hit registration is instantaneous at slash resolution, evaluated by walking the released polyline point-by-point — there is no swept active window an enemy can dodge into or out of — and resolution walks the paperdoll part list FRONT-to-BACK so the topmost part struck decides the hit (which is the actual mechanism behind 'shielder legs / undead heads' weak points).

new_findings.text: The v0.717 desktop build carries the same per-stance slash-length switch as the android bundle but with different constants — Light/Reversed x1.4, Balanced x(1+0.02*mastery), Heavy x(0.5+0.04*mastery) floored at 100, Dual x1.0 floored at 100 — so all three multipliers moved between builds and the android values must not be shipped.
new_findings.ledger_text: **The stance tables (dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4, reach 300/200/100) are MASTERY-9 CEILING values, not base.**
new_findings.lane_impact: combat-core L2: the per-stance reach multipliers become CONTRACT for v0.717 at 1.4 / 1+0.02m / 0.5+0.04m, replacing the android 1.5 / 1+0.005m / 0.5+0.005m that the rebirth survey published. Also refutes that survey's claim that no desktop counterpart could be found.

new_findings.text: Stance mastery is a skill level with exactly ten levels (skills 1000/1001/1002 have 10 <level> blocks, max value 10), not a 0-100 percentage, and both builds gate FlipUp/Deflect/Launch/Stab on it at 3/4/5.

new_findings.text: Elemental damage is added AFTER the defense subtraction and its minDamage floor, so DEF has no effect on elemental damage at all — there is no elemental ATK-vs-DEF formula to find.

Also feeds L1 combat-core: the damage pipeline is (roll minus DEF, floored at minDamage) plus the sum of four elemental terms, all unmitigated.

new_findings.quote: §c-2: Light plateau 233-241, max 303 (n=17) · Balanced 116-131, max 131 (n=17) · Heavy plateau 97-103, max 121 (n=25). Payload: baseSlashLength = 120 + Math.floor((90 + Dan*5) * speed / (20 + speed)); slashModifier Light 1.5 / Balanced 1+0.005m / Heavy 0.5+0.005m. RATIO TEST PASSES: payload Light/Heavy at mastery 0 = 1.5/0.5 = 3.00; frame, same level-8 character = 303/100 = 3.03. MAGNITUDE TEST FAILS: both frame readings imply base ≈ 202 (303/1.5 = 202; 100/0.5 = 200), and inverting 120 + floor(90*s/(20+s)) = 202 needs s ≈ 205, while the web per-stat cap at level 8 is 1+(8+10)*3 = 55 and the whole formula's Dan-0 asymptote is 210.

Separately, the 3.00-vs-3.03 ratio match is a genuine independent cross-validation of both artifacts and should be recorded as such.

verdicts.reason: The interpretation is exactly backwards. So the lane_impact 'prevents mis-wiring the border colour to the 4-tier rarity ladder; border tracks <unique>, text colour tracks the 4 tiers' is false on both halves - the border IS the 4-tier ladder, purple is its unique branch, blue is its rare branch. Further, purple is not <unique>1: Item.as:392-395 returns "unique" also for pickable quest items, the five trade-quest IDs (20103-20107) and any player-named item. The A1 half survives - I re-sampled the border over (1270,600)-(1460,775) and the modal saturated purple is RGB(144,102,203), matching - but the reading does not.

verdicts.reason: The floor DOES live in the generic damage pipeline, which is precisely what the claim denies. Damage.getMinDamage() applies the identical four-band ladder keyed to attackerlvl: if(attackerlvl<=10) return 1+piercingDamage; if(<=20) return attackerlvl/8+piercing; if(<=30) return attackerlvl/6+piercing; return attackerlvl/4+piercing. Damage is the object every hit is delivered through. Because it keys on the ATTACKER's level, an enemy hitting the player floors at literally EnemyLevel/4 in the top band - so the ledger's bullet is RIGHT in variable and only INCOMPLETE in shape (one of four bands). The surveyor's playerLVL version is the mirror case with the player as attacker, and it is not 'boss auto-scaling' either: the same block appears in at least five enemy classes (EnemyElite.as:63, EnemyKanjiGuardian.as:88, EnemyWolfAlpha.as:109, EnemySpearElite.as:107, EnemyPlayer.as:120). Correct correction is 'one band of a four-band ATTACKER-level floor, 1 / lvl8 / lvl6 / lvl4, plus piercingDamage', not 'wrong in both variable and shape'.
verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/Damage.as:149-171 (getMinDamage, attackerlvl four-band ladder); corroborating sites EnemyElite.as:63, EnemyKanjiGuardian.as:88, EnemyWolfAlpha.as:109, EnemySpearElite.as:107, EnemyPlayer.as:107-123

new_findings.lane_impact: L5 (UI/HUD) + L6 (art) - a builder needs eight border states, not a purple flag; and the border must be wired to the SAME derived-rarity function as the name colour. This directly overturns the surveyor's items-equipment/purple-border-is-unique-not-rarity lane guidance.

new_findings.text: The generic damage pipeline carries a four-band minimum-damage floor keyed to the ATTACKER's level - 1 / lvl8 / lvl6 / lvl4, each plus piercingDamage - which is what the ledger's 'EnemyLevel/4' bullet actually refers to when an enemy strikes the player.
new_findings.quote: public function getMinDamage() : int { if(this.damage == 0) { return 0; } if(this.attackerlvl == 0) { return this.damage; } if(this.attackerlvl <= 10) { return 1 + this.piercingDamage; } if(this.attackerlvl <= 20) { return this.attackerlvl / 8 + this.piercingDamage; } if(this.attackerlvl <= 30) { return this.attackerlvl / 6 + this.piercingDamage; } return this.attackerlvl / 4 + this.piercingDamage; }
new_findings.ledger_text: defense min-floor (EnemyLevel/4)
new_findings.lane_impact: L1/L2 (combat core + damage) - the ledger bullet is correct-but-incomplete, not wrong; it needs three more bands and a piercingDamage term. The enemy-class copies (EnemyElite/KanjiGuardian/WolfAlpha/SpearElite/Player) are the same ladder with the player as attacker, used for HP auto-scaling.

verdicts.reason: The mechanism is HELD and the design conclusion ('betting is not a gold faucet') is RIGHT — but the stated reason is wrong, and in a direction that makes the conclusion stronger. Dice are fair: InteractUI.as:1811-1812 two independent int(Math.random()*6) over {0..5}, :1823 isEven = (dice1+dice2)%2==0, so P(even)=0.5 exactly. But the two sides of the wager use different functions. The stake at doBet :1796 is 'StatsManager.changeStat(StatsManager.STAT_GOLD,-num)' — uncapped. The payout at :1834 is 'StatsManager.changeGold(this.bet * 2)' — and changeGold (StatsManager.as:2658-2667) clamps to getMaxCoins() and silently discards the overflow. With the default purse cap of 1000 (StatsManager.as:2637), any bet whose doubled return would cross the cap is a guaranteed partial loss. Cho-Han is EV-NEGATIVE near the cap, not EV-neutral.
verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/InteractUI.as:1790-1844 read in full, cross-referenced to StatsManager.as:2632-2667 (getMaxCoins / changeGold clamp)

new_findings.lane_impact: L0 enemies-ai, and the biggest thing this unit missed. Blocker (1) is closed for trash but only half-closed for bosses: there are TWO formulas and the surveyor found one, so the 78 is over-scored on that axis. Boss HP is set so the player needs 10 + lvlDiff hits (floor 3) and boss ATK so the player dies in 18 - lvlDiff hits (floor 1); authored <hp> is only a floor, which qualifies the roster claim. Critically, src/config/combat-sim.ts documents ENEMY_BASE as INFERRED with 'B4 makes hp and minDamage DERIVED at spawn from the player's own stats (enemyHP = effPlayerDmg x K) ... the pre-scale floor the source's max(scaledBase, ...) compares against' -- bossHP = playerhit * hitsToKillBoss IS that formula and if(bossHP > maxhp) IS that max(). K = 10 + (enemyLvl - playerLvl), floored at 3. That INFERRED comment can be promoted to A2, labelled v0.682-ANDROID.

new_findings.text: The War-Room tick is 3600 real seconds (one hour), not 24 hours, so REBUILD_READINESS.md's one concrete number for the 'day' blocker is wrong by 24x.
new_findings.ledger_text: - **The real-world "day" length** governing quest expiry, farming, AP regen, and the War-Room 24h tick.
new_findings.lane_impact: L1 world-exploration and L11 meta-social: strengthens the surveyor's blocker-(3) refutation from 'mis-framed' to 'contains a factually wrong number'. The war turn is hourly and timestamp-based off QueryManager.getServerTime(), and it persists in save slot 102 (nextWarTurn). Any war-room port that assumed a daily tick is 24x too slow.

new_findings.text: A fifth independent real-time clock exists that the 'three clocks' claim omits: duel-token regen runs on a 120-second interval.
new_findings.lane_impact: L1 world-exploration and L11 meta-social: the correct count is at least five clocks - AP 60 s, duel tokens 120 s, war turn 3600 s, crops 900/3600/21600/43200 s, quest repeat 86400 s. Duel tokens start at 20 (STAT_DUELTOKENS/STAT_MAXDUELTOKENS, StatsManager.as:709-710) and persist via save slot 101.

new_findings.text: The 12-hour crop (plantType 4) has no ROTTED branch at all - once ready it stays harvestable forever, so the '15-minute grace before ROT' rule applies only to the 15 min / 1 h / 6 h crops.
new_findings.lane_impact: L1 world-exploration: corrects the surveyor's farming table before it reaches src/config. Types 1-3 all carry the explicit three-way ladder gated on timePeriod + gracePeriod; type 4 is two-way. Porting a uniform rot rule would destroy the 12 h crop's only advantage.

new_findings.text: AP == 0 in adventure mode is not a death or retreat condition - it swaps the player to a TIRED idle animation, and the same branch fires in combat at HP <= 25% of max.
new_findings.lane_impact: L1 world-exploration (removes a fabricated rule from the AP claim) and L6 art-anim-audio-feel (adds a real, uncatalogued one). TIRED appears exactly twice in the class - here and in a sheathed-state test at :4319 - so it is unambiguously an idle pose, not a state transition. The combat half is the more valuable half: the fighter visibly changes idle at quarter health, which is a feel cue the art lane can implement.

new_findings.text: Max AP is not hard-capped at level+30: level+30 is only the stat-point spend ceiling, and equipment adds on top via findBonusStat(STAT_MAXAP).
new_findings.lane_impact: L1 world-exploration and L4 items-equipment: the regen loop stops at base MAXAP + gear bonus, so AP-boosting equipment raises the real ceiling above level+30. Two separate numbers that must not be collapsed into one config constant.

new_findings.text: TerritoryData.getNorthExits contains a dead branch: rng.rand(3) can only return 0, 1 or 2, but the code tests dice == 3 to set count = 2 - so every territory generates exactly one north exit.
new_findings.lane_impact: L1 world-exploration: a latent bug in the original world generator, not a design choice. Because rnd() returns [0,1), rand(3) is confined to {0,1,2}. A faithful 1:1 port must decide explicitly whether to reproduce the bug (always 1 exit) or the evident intent (sometimes 2) - and must say which. Worth checking the sibling getSouth/East/WestExits for the same pattern.

verdicts.reason: Cite resolves and the quote is verbatim, but the headline number is wrong for one of the two shutters and the stated arithmetic is fabricated. I simulated update() exactly as decompiled (++counter, then y += speed, then speed += 2): the speed used on frame n is 2(n-1), so displacement after n frames is n(n-1), NOT (n-2)(n-1). It reaches 240 px at n=16. TRANSITION_BLACKCLOSE therefore closes geometrically at frame 16 and only takes 17 frames because of the `counter >= 17` gate at :87 -- so 17 frames / 708 ms is right, but not for the reason given. TRANSITION_BLACKOPEN (:93-108) has NO counter gate; its only exit is `blackup.y <= -240`, which my simulation fires at frame 16 -> 667 ms. So 'each black shutter takes 17 frames (708 ms)' is false: close = 17, open = 16. The white fade (24 frames / 1000 ms) survives, and the 24 fps it converts at is independently confirmed -- I read the SWF header of reference/decrypted/shs3_android_payload_decoded.swf: framerate fixed8 6144 = 24.0 fps, stage rect 800x480 px.

verdicts.reason: The measurements hold — I confirmed 471 <choice>, 0 with <outcome>, 7 with <condition>, 0 <gotolabel>. The CONCLUSION is false. Consequence is carried by WHERE a choice jumps, not by the choice element. <goto> is an index into the flattened display list (XMLQuestStep.getXMLIntroList pushes one entry per intro child, plus one null slot per <choice>; CutsceneManager.gotoStep sets currentDisplayNo = goto), so a branch can land before or after a state-writing <outcome>. Worked case at questdata.xml:814-882: the choice '(FIghting Tutorial) I may be able to learn something here.' (goto 14) routes through <outcome> id=113 set=8402944, id=114 set=4, id=102 set=0, while the sibling 'I should go.' (goto 19) routes to <outcome><modify>0</modify><end>1</end> and writes nothing. I simulated all 196 options against the real interpreter semantics: 55 of 196 have choices whose branches differ in state written or in terminal (leaveOK vs leaveCancel) — e.g. Prologue step 9 'Let's start mining.' sets 113/114/115/102 vs 'Not right now.' none; Prologue step 14 sets 110=12 on one branch only; Fighting Tutorial step 3 sets 30017=3 on one branch only. The lane guidance 'a flat jump table, not a consequence system ... drops a large chunk of L1's assumed runtime risk' is the dangerous half and would mis-build the quest state machine.

verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/ScreenTransition.as:76-105,110,143-146,159-162 (simulated tick-by-tick) + SWF header of reference/decrypted/shs3_android_payload_decoded.swf (stage 0,800,0,480 px; framerate 24.0)
verdicts.reason: The claim's entire value is the word 'exactly', and the exact numbers are wrong. startClose seeds y=-240, speed=0; update() does ++counter; y += speed; speed += 2. Displacement after n ticks is n(n-1), NOT the (n-2)(n-1) the claim states. n(n-1)=240 at n=16, so the shutters physically meet on tick 16, not 17; `counter >= 17` merely withholds doAction() one extra tick. startOpen (:159-162) has NO counter gate — doAction fires the same tick displacement reaches 240, i.e. tick 16 / 667 ms. So 'EACH black shutter takes 17 frames' is false for the open shutter and mislabels an action gate as the shutter for the close one. The two off-by-ones in the surveyor's derivation cancel to produce 240, which is why the arithmetic looks closed. White fade: alpha starts at 1 (:174) and -=1/24; in IEEE-754 doubles the residue after 24 ticks is +3.75e-16 so `alpha <= 0` first holds on tick 25; under AVM2's 1/256 alpha quantisation it lands on 24 — 'exactly 24' is not established either way. What DOES survive and I confirmed independently: 24.0 fps and the 800x480 stage, read straight from the SWF header. Cite lines are off by one in three of four places (:79 not :80, :110 not :111, :142 not :143).

verdicts.reason: The quotes are verbatim but the arithmetic and the word 'each' are wrong. (a) The stated formula (n-2)(n-1) is false. Speed applies then increments, so frame n adds 2(n-1) and cumulative displacement is n(n-1), which reaches 240 at n=16. I simulated the loop exactly as written: close frame 16 y=0 (shutters MEET), close frame 17 DOACTION. So BLACKCLOSE is 16 frames of motion (667 ms) plus one held frame before the action (708 ms) — two numbers, not one, and the claimed formula does not produce either. (b) 'Each black shutter takes 17 frames' is false for the open shutter: TRANSITION_BLACKOPEN (ScreenTransition.as:93-107) has NO counter gate and fires doAction the instant blackup.y <= -240 — simulated: open frame 16 DOACTION = 16 frames / 667 ms. A rebuild shipping 708 ms for both is wrong on every room exit. (c) The white fade half HOLDS (1/24 per frame from alpha 1 -> 0 on frame 24 = 1000 ms), but only because startOpenWhite has exactly one caller (Overworld.as:377) passing ACTION_REFRESHROOMONOPEN, whose case at :289-292 re-arms transitioning=true; otherwise doAction() at counter==2 would freeze the fade at alpha 0.917. That coupling must be copied. Parity is fine — web build's own copy at shs3_payload/scripts/§1t6497s0§.as:79-124 is structurally identical.

Cumulative displacement after n frames is n(n-1), which is 240 at n=16 — NOT (n-2)(n-1). BLACKOPEN at :98-107 has no counter test at all.
new_findings.lane_impact: L-ui-hud: corrects the survey's 'each shutter = 17 frames / 708 ms' to open=16/667 and close=16 motion + action at 17/708. A rebuild shipping 708 ms for the open shutter is wrong on every room exit. Also banks the white-fade coupling: startOpenWhite has exactly one caller (Overworld.as:377) passing ACTION_REFRESHROOMONOPEN, whose case at :289-292 re-arms transitioning=true — without that pairing the counter==2 doAction would freeze the fade at alpha 0.917.

new_findings.text: Skill-slot hotkey numbers are assigned right-to-left by initKeyPressText(slotCount - i) against a right-to-left layout, which reproduces the filmed HUD exactly — three slots, leftmost empty and unnumbered because its skillSlots entry is null, middle key 2, right key 3.

verdicts.reason: The artifact is real and the goblin numbers are right, but the rule is generalized and the generalization is false. The cite asserts the selection rule is 'mirrored in every Enemy* class'. It is not: only EnemyGoblin, EnemyGoblinThrower and EnemyZombie carry their own gore branch; the other 31 Enemy* classes extend NPC, and NPC.as:898 'override public function die()' runs a DIFFERENT dice — NPC.as:1005 'dice = Math.random() * 7;' giving <=1 ENEMYDEATH (2/7), ==2 DEATH_FORWARD, ==3 DEFEATED2 (if !isRedFreeze), ==4 ENEMYDEATHNOHAND, ==5 DEATHINHALF, else ENEMYDEATH + createFlyingWeapon() + createFlyingHat(). So 40/20/20/20 is the goblin distribution, not the game's; the human-opponent path is a 7-way split containing two animations (DEATH_FORWARD, DEFEATED2) that appear nowhere in the goblin branch. This is the path that matters — the frame I opened shows a human enemy felled, not a goblin, and the game is a samurai duelling game. A recreation built to 40/20/20/20 ships the wrong distribution and drops the flying-weapon/flying-hat beat. Everything else in the claim verified exactly: 8 death anims in 108_1t4635s0.bin with deathnohand=25, deathnohead=31, deathinhalf=28; the 50% mirror; StatsManager.as:314 'public static var censored:Boolean = false;'.

verdicts.reason: This claim invokes the standing FRAME-WINS invariant, so it must be right, and it isn't. The quote reproduces GameEngine.as lines 269 and 270 and stops — line 271 is 'var originalHeightWithBar:int = 690;' and line 278 is 'originalHeight = originalHeightWithBar;', guarded by :275 'if(newAspectRatio <= originalWithBarAspectRatio)' and setting :279 'StatsManager.stageShowingFriendBar = true;'. So 800x690 is not 'container chrome': it is an explicitly named alternate canvas — the friend-bar layout — that the same function switches to when the window is narrower than 800/690. The disconfirming line sits one line below the last line quoted. Consequently there is NO frame-vs-doc disagreement to arbitrate: the payload declares both heights, the SWF document rect was authored at the with-bar height, and the frame merely shows a session in the wide mode. 'THE FRAME WINS over the SWF document rect' misapplies the invariant to a conflict that does not exist. Two further defects: (1) the arithmetic does not close — I reproduced the measurement (cols 52..1867, w 1816, aspect 1.681481) but 1816/1080 = 1.6815 while 800/480 = 1.6667; a true 800x480 surface at 1080 tall would be 1800 px wide, not 1816, so the frame lands ~0.9% off 5:3 rather than equalling it, and their 'thr 12' label is off by one pixel (thr 12 gives w 1817 in my run; w 1816 appears at thr 25/40/60). (2) The letterbox formula is Android-only — grep for originalWidth/originalHeight over reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/ returns ZERO hits — so an Android constant is used to settle a web capture without the Android-parity caveat this same survey rightly enforces on audio. What survives and should be kept: 800x480 is the play-field canvas and 800x690 is the friend-bar layout, both payload constants, so re-basing HUD fractions on 800x480 is still the right instruction.
