new_findings.lane_impact: art-anim-audio-feel: blocker ⑤ is closed, but with THIS distribution, not the goblin one. 31 of 34 Enemy* classes inherit it (only EnemyGoblin, EnemyGoblinThrower and EnemyZombie override). new_findings.text: The '150% DAMAGE' text visible in the duel HUD is a timed consumable buff readout, not the stance modifier and not the behead multiplier — it is one of a family of buff strings driven by bufftype.

new_findings.text: The stance rock-paper-scissors damage multiplier is x1.2, not x1.5, and a stance-advantage hit recolours its damage popup to white.
new_findings.quote: MCSPlayer.as:3701 `if(this.stance == LIGHT_STANCE && enemyStance == BALANCED_STANCE || this.stance == BALANCED_STANCE && enemyStance == HEAVY_STANCE || this.stance == HEAVY_STANCE && enemyStance == LIGHT_STANCE)` :3703 `damage *= 1.2;` :3705 `damagetextcol = 16777215;`
new_findings.lane_impact: combat-core: the stance triangle is Light>Balanced>Heavy>Light at a flat x1.2, applied BEFORE defence subtraction and before the x1.5 behead multiplier (order: x1.2, then -= getDefense(), then min-damage clamp, then x1.5 if behead). ui-hud: 0xFFFFFF is the stance-advantage damage-popup colour, a byte-exact HUD value nobody holds.

new_findings.text: 800x690 is not container chrome — it is `originalHeightWithBar`, a named second canvas the engine switches to when the window is narrower than 800/690, which also turns the friend panel on.
new_findings.quote: GameEngine.as:271 `var originalHeightWithBar:int = 690;` :273 `var originalWithBarAspectRatio:Number = originalWidth / originalHeightWithBar;` :275 `if(newAspectRatio <= originalWithBarAspectRatio)` :278 `originalHeight = originalHeightWithBar;` :279 `StatsManager.stageShowingFriendBar = true;` … :311-312 `StatsManager.stageBaseWidth = originalWidth; StatsManager.stageBaseHeight = originalHeight;`
new_findings.ledger_text: **Aspect-ratio truth** — native canvas is **800×480 (5:3)**, so HUD x-fractions measured off 16:9 video may be pillarbox-wrong.
new_findings.lane_impact: art-anim-audio-feel and ui-hud: the ledger's open item closes as TWO payload contracts, not one. 800x480 is the play-field canvas; 800x690 is the friend-bar layout, and the 210 px difference is a social panel, which is why the web SWF document rect is authored at 690. HUD fractions must be re-based on 800x480 AND the recreation must decide whether it ships the friend bar at all. There is no frame-vs-doc conflict to invoke the FRAME-WINS invariant over. Caveat: this formula exists only in the Android bundle — grep over reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/ for originalWidth/originalHeight returns zero hits — so it inherits the S0-3 Android-parity caveat.

Note indices 8 (crotch) and 17 (hat) are declared but never written by the light-stance blob — they are driven elsewhere (the hat is a separate detachable, see createFlyingHat).

new_findings.text: The screen-shake amplitude parameter is effectively dead for every in-game trigger: because shakeAmount = min(amt, counter) and every hard-coded call passes a duration of 24 or less against a default amt of 30, the amplitude is always just the remaining tick count — a pure linear ramp-down from the duration value.
new_findings.cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/StageManager.as:1200, :1225; call sites HeavenlySwordProjectile.as:76, MCSPlayer.as:911/:946/:4180, Trap_CrusherColumnAuto.as:90, Trap_CrusherBlockAuto.as:88, StatsManager.as:3535, Marker_RumbleTrigger.as:44
new_findings.quote: StageManager.as:1200 `startShake(shakeDuration:int, shakeAmt:int = 30)` · :1225 `shakeAmount = Math.min(screenShakeAmt,screenShakeCounter);` · all hard-coded calls pass duration only: `startShake(12)` x3, `startShake(24)`, `startShake(6)` x2 — so amt=30 is never the binding term
new_findings.ledger_text: ④ **screen-shake** + **hitstop-on-landed-hit** (never catalogued);
new_findings.lane_impact: art-anim-audio-feel: sharpens blocker ④. The recreation should implement shake as `offset = uniform(-t/2, +t/2)` on both axes where t is the REMAINING tick count — a 12-tick Cleave shake starts at ±5.5 px and decays to 0, it never reaches ±15. The 30 default only ever binds through Marker_RumbleTrigger's data-driven amt. Also the full trigger set is 8 call sites, three more than the survey listed: HeavenlySwordProjectile.as:76 (12), Trap_CrusherBlockAuto.as:88 (6), StatsManager.as:3535 (data-driven).

new_findings.lane_impact: art-anim-audio-feel: the survey measured two blobs and generalized; the generalization is correct and now proven exhaustively. Every hold in the game is code-injected by AnimData's per-animation duration tail and held by the frameList.length guard in MCSCharacter.updateFrame — none of it is authored into the data. This is a directly testable invariant: a rebuild importing these blobs can assert `@d == len(<f>)` as a data-integrity gate.

verdicts.reason: Conclusion HELD, but the METHOD as cited cannot support it and I had to prove it properly. An AS3 grep cannot see blend modes: in Flash they are authored in the IDE and stored in the PlaceObject3 tag's PlaceFlagHasBlendMode bit, with no code involved. I therefore wrote a recursive DefineSprite walker and read flags2>>1&1 on every PlaceObject3 in every container: web payload 304, android payload 248, SHS3Resource 12, BGResource 54, ImageResource 1473 — ZERO with a blend mode set, 2,091 tags total. So the negative now holds at byte level AND in the WEB build, which the grep could not give it. ColorCode.as confirmed verbatim (ColorTransform, BlurFilter, the 0.3/0.59/0.11 luma ColorMatrixFilter, setMCTint). My grep for blendMode across ALL decompiled bundles returns exactly 3 hits, all mx/core/IFlexDisplayObject.as — matching the claim. ONE cite correction: the cite lists reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/ as if it were web CLIENT code. It is not — StageManager, MCSPlayer, SoundManager, ColorCode, AnimData, GameEngine, StatsManager and EnemyGoblin are ALL absent from that bundle (it holds only art/framework classes). Every AS3 claim in this survey is Android-only, not just the audio ones.
verdicts.own_cite: my recursive PlaceObject3 blend-mode scan over reference/decrypted/shs3_payload_decoded.swf + shs3_android_payload_decoded.swf + my decodes of 115/120/124 (0 of 2,091 tags set HasBlendMode); reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/ColorCode.as:12-120; `ls reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/StageManager.as` -> absent

verdicts.reason: Algorithm confirmed verbatim at StageManager.as:1200-1227: startShake(shakeDuration, shakeAmt = 30) captures screenShakeStartPos; doShake decrements, snaps back exactly at counter==0, else shakeAmount = Math.min(screenShakeAmt, screenShakeCounter) and offsets both axes by -amt/2 + random()*amt. Confirmed too that update() calls doShake() BEFORE the 'if(actionState != STATE_FROZEN)' gate at :826-830, so the shake really does keep running while the action is frozen. But 'fully catalogued' over-claims the trigger set: grep -rn 'startShake(' returns EIGHT call sites, not the five listed. Missed: Trap_CrusherBlockAuto.as:88 (6), HeavenlySwordProjectile.as:76 (12), and StatsManager.as:3535 'startShake(val)' — a fully data-driven duration whose value is not a literal at all.
verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/StageManager.as:1200-1227 and :824-830; my `grep -rn "startShake(" reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/` returning 8 call sites incl. Trap_CrusherBlockAuto.as:88, HeavenlySwordProjectile.as:76, StatsManager.as:3535

verdicts.reason: The measurement half is CORRECT and I strengthened it — I parsed every animation in all 19 web animdata blobs and @d equals the <f> count for ALL 487, zero mismatches (the survey demonstrated only a four-anim sample). But the stated MECHANISM is wrong for 21% of the data. The claim says the latch 'is injected in code by AnimData's per-animation duration tails, which the frame guard then holds on the final pose.' That is only the non-looping path. 102 of the 487 animations carry a THIRD attribute the survey never noticed: l="1". It is parsed at AnimData.as:16 'this.looping = xml.@l == 1;' (field declared :10) and consumed at MCSCharacter.as:1293 'this.currentAnimationLooping = this.currentAnimation.looping;'. The looping set is precisely the motion a rebuild cares most about: lightstanceidle, balancedstanceidle, heavystanceidle, walk, run_sheathed, lightstancerun, balancedstancerun, heavystancerun, ninjastealthwalk, every *_partb slash tail, all creature idles/walks/runs, mining, femalewalk. Those CYCLE; they do not latch on the final pose. A rebuild following this claim as written will freeze the idle. Secondary: the Mobile.as:117 cite is mis-framed — 'GameEngine.getStageMC().frameRate = 24;' sits inside 'if(GameEngine.getStageMC().frameRate == 0)' at :113, i.e. a fallback, not the setting. 24 Hz is nonetheless correct: every SWF header I parsed (shs3.swf, both payloads, all five resource blobs, SHS1, SHS2) reads framerate=24.0.

verdicts.reason: The CONCLUSION (design canvas = 800x480) is correct, but all three pillars of this claim fail. (a) ARITHMETIC: I reproduced the measurement exactly (thr 25/40/60 -> cols 52..1867, w=1816, aspect=1.681481) and the claim then asserts '1.6815 = 800x480'. 800/480 = 1.666667. A true 800x480 surface letterboxed into 1080 px of height is 1800 px wide, not 1816 — the frame is 0.89% WIDER than 800x480 predicts (8 px per side; sub-pixel edge analysis of the column means narrows it to ~1814, still != 1800). So the frame does NOT confirm 800x480; it lands near it. Under §0 that has to be said, not rounded away. verdicts.reason: The window is NOT 'a single uniform 12-tick window ... set identically in every enemy class and in MCSPlayer'. My census of every assignment returns SEVEN distinct values across 32 sites: 12 (x23), 24 (x2), 16, 26, 84, 0 (x3), -1. verdicts.reason: The 6.0 s number is wrong, and the surveyor's own quote contains the disproof. Setup is redFreezeCounter = 24*6 = 144 (StageManager.as:1101), but the terminator at :916 fires at 'redFreezeCounter == 24' (not 0), setting redFreezeCounter = -2 and calling GameEngine.endBattleMode(true). So the normal victory beat is 144-24 = 120 ticks = 5.0 s; 6.0 s occurs only in the branch where the player is still playing SHEATHESWORDCHIBURI. The frame agrees with 5.0, not 6.0: COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS §S24-F's measured kill-cam is 'red screen total ~74 ticks (~4.9 s)' at the 15 fps floor — so the measurement and the code agree once the code is read correctly, and only the claim is out. Second error in the same claim: the actor freeze is RELEASED at 24*5 by unRedFreeze() — the same tick showWin() fires. MCSActor.redFreeze() is 'ColorCode.makeBlack(mcs); animFrozen = true' and unRedFreeze() is 'animFrozen = false', so the black-silhouette hold lasts 1.0 s, not 6.0; the remaining ~4 s is an input-disabled result screen. A recreation holding the silhouette six seconds is 6x wrong.

verdicts.reason: The central assertion is false. I measured @d vs len(<f>) across all 19 web-payload animdata blobs myself: 96 of 385 parseable <anim> rows have @d > the number of <f> children, INCLUDING in both files the surveyor names as evidence. 108_1t4635s0.bin has 23 mismatches (heavyhorizontalslash_parta d=6 with 4 <f>); 118_1t4645s0.bin has 6 (light_horslash_parta d=13 with 11 <f>; light_horslash_partc d=6 with 4); 116_1t4643s0.bin has heavy_horslash_parta d=5 with only 2 <f>, i.e. 60% of that animation is a held pose. Every horizontal/down/up slash is not. The engine confirms the opposite semantics: AnimData.as:16-21 sets duration = xml.@d and frameList from xml.f independently, MCSCharacter updateAnimation runs frameCounter to currentAnimationDuration, and updateFrame only re-poses `if(frameCounter < frameList.length)` — so every tick in [len(frameList), duration) is a DATA-AUTHORED hold on the last keyframe. The AnimData duration += 10/15/24 tails are a second hold stacked on top, not the origin of the latch. A recreation on the surveyor's model plays heavy_horslash_parta 2.5x too fast. The 24 Hz half is correct and I verified it independently (my own SWF header parse of reference/preservation/shs3.swf: framerate 24.0; Mobile.as:117).

I re-ran the threshold sweep on the same frame and reproduced the numbers exactly (thr 25/40/60 -> cols 52..1867, w 1816, aspect 1.68148), but 800/480 = 1.66667 and a true 5:3 surface at 1080 tall is 1800 px wide, not 1816. The extra 210 px is the game's OWN friend panel — a responsive layout mode it draws, not browser chrome. new_findings.lane_impact: L-combat-core: the stance triangle is a x1.2 multiplier applied BEFORE defense subtraction, and the behead x1.5 is applied AFTER the minimum-damage clamp — an ordering no ledger holds and one that changes low-damage outcomes materially. new_findings.text: The web and Android war-room wave tables agree on 39 waves and 351 total enemies but not on composition: seven late waves in the web build draw from a five-slot id pool that includes an extra id 443, which the Android build reduces to two slots.
new_findings.ledger_text: kill cap 350
new_findings.lane_impact: L0 meta-social / enemies-ai — the 351 kill total is safe from either build, but the per-wave enemy MIX must be read from the web file (bindata/119); the Android copy is a different, thinner draw.

result.score_rationale: Not a system sweep — no re-score submitted. For context on the ledger's own numbers: skilldata alone closes or downgrades six named blockers (skills-meters ② and ④; rebirth-elements ① and half of ②; ui-hud ④; plus an unlisted enemies-ai behaviour gap), and refutes two ledger "Surface" verdicts (chi costs single-digit; elements are two unlinked systems). skills-meters at 33 and rebirth-elements at 30 are the two thinnest scores in the document and both are materially wrong on the low side. The one place the ledger is right and I confirm it: Focus numerics and the crit proc rule are genuinely absent from this source.

claims.text: reference/extracted/skilldata.xml (web v0.717) and reference/extracted/android/117_Mobile_SkillData.bin (Android v0.682) are the same file modulo line endings — 75 skills, identical ids and identical normalized bodies — so the Stage-0b S0-3 build-parity caveat does not apply to any skill number or string.

claims.text: The SPD-to-cooldown formula is not missing: cooldown multiplier = 1 - min(SPD,300)/300 * 0.5, i.e. SPD is hard-capped at 300 and the maximum possible cooldown reduction is exactly 50%, with the speed buff multiplying SPD by 1.5 before the cap.

claims.lane_impact: skills-meters — blocker ④ closed with an exact formula; combat-core; items-equipment — SPD-modifier gear now has a quantified effect.

claims.text: <cooldown> is in seconds and the engine multiplies it by 24 to get internal frames — the OG runs at 24 FPS, so every duration recovered from this payload (cooldowns and every animation d= value) converts to this repo's fixed 60Hz Sim at x2.5, not x1 or x2.

result.score_rationale: Not a system sweep — no re-score issued. For the record, npcdata alone moves enemies-ai well above its 34: blockers ① (level→stat formula) and ② (per-enemy HP) are both closed by exact data, and the 38-class AI taxonomy is recovered whole; blockers ③/④/⑤ stay open but are now localised to 38 named ActionScript classes rather than "unknown". economy ① and rebirth-elements ② are also closed from this one file, and items-equipment ⑤ (sprite-compositing contract) is closed by the MCSCharacter bone tree. The single most damaging remaining ledger error in this lane is the "9-slot paperdoll" figure (it is 12 mcs slots / a 13-wide equipment vector) and the "4 clans" figure (npcdata ships five identical 57-NPC clan armies).

claims.text: The 63×72 map bitmap and the 12-bit territory-ID space are at different scales and I could not reconcile which unit getPlaceName is called with — stated as open rather than resolved.
claims.quote: NameGenerator.as:147 `var namex:int = territoryx % 137;` — a modulo by 137 is only meaningful if territory-x can exceed 137, which is wider than the 63-cell width of the map bitmap. The two hardcoded constants (NameGenerator.as:137-144) decode arithmetically to (343,344) and (372,333), also outside 63x72 — though both land near territory (57,57) if read as NODE ids and divided by the 6x subdivision. I am not asserting a resolution.

result.score_rationale: Source lane, not a system lane — no re-score submitted. But the itemdata sweep alone moves three system floors hard: progression's headline blocker (L11–80 XP curve) is dead, economy's blocker ① (coins-per-kill AND the XP formula) is dead, and items-equipment blockers ①/④ are now fully closed (Pass 1 closed ②/③/⑤). §6's "structurally UNRECOVERABLE" list loses its second entry (L11–80 XP curve) after verbatim dialogue. Counterweight: I found the first hard proof that the Android v0.682 bundle and the web v0.717 bundle DISAGREE on tuning constants (rebirth gold 5/20 vs 25/100; guest heavenly gold 0 vs 3), so every Android-sourced number now needs a build label — that is a real cost against the confidence of any lane that ported Android AS3 constants this run.

result.score_rationale: Source sweep, not a system sweep — no re-score issued. Run 1 (2026-08-15) already banked 23 questdata claims and is preserved verbatim in the journal; this run re-read the file end-to-end independently, confirmed run-1's headlines (Q-01/02/03/14/15), and adds 10 claims run 1 did not have, including two corrections to run 1 itself.
